q: 68. Resource smoothening means
options: adjustment of resources to have the least variations
complete renovation if resources suit the requirement
optimization and economical utilization of resources
explain: Resource smoothening rearranges non-critical activities within their float to minimize fluctuations in resource demand while keeping project duration fixed.

q: 69. In the time-cost optimization using CPM, the crashing of the activities along the critical path is done starting with the activity having
explain: Crashing begins with the activity having the least (lowest) cost slope, as it gives the maximum time reduction per unit extra cost.

q: 70. When all the paths are arranged according to the descending order of the float, the path which is next to critical path is known as
explain: The path with the next-lowest float after the critical path (zero float) is termed the secondary critical path.

q: 71. Which of the following is a dummy activity?
options: Await the arrival of concrete material
explain: Waiting for material arrival is a logical constraint/dependency with no resource consumption of its own, characteristic of a dummy activity.

q: 72. The opening of bidding in the process of procurement is known as
explain: Tendering is the process by which bids are invited and opened in procurement.

q: 73. The first stage of a construction, is
explain: Construction begins with the initiation of the proposal/idea, before surveys, estimates, or fund allotment occur.

q: 74. Pre-tender stage requires
options: finalization of designs and preparation of estimate
explain: The pre-tender stage specifically requires finalizing designs and preparing detailed estimates before the tender is floated.

q: 75. The main function of the construction management is
explain: Construction management encompasses all managerial functions - planning, organizing, and directing - to achieve project objectives.

q: 76. Construction team means
explain: A construction team comprises the owner, engineer/architect, and contractor working together to complete the project.

q: 77. A golden rule for the procurement of construction stores, suggests
options: 67% at the site and 33% under procurement
50% at the site and 50% under procurement
33% at the site and 67% under procurement
explain: The conventional guideline for stores management suggests keeping about two-thirds (67%) of material at site and one-third (33%) in the procurement pipeline.

q: 78. Military organisation is known as
explain: Military organizations follow a strict chain-of-command structure characteristic of line organization.

q: 79. The main advantage of line organization, is
explain: Line organization provides clear command, defined responsibilities, and strong discipline - all being its key advantages.

q: 80. Frederick W. Taylor introduced a system of working know as
explain: F.W. Taylor introduced functional organization, dividing management functions among specialists.

q: 81. The most popular type of organization used for civil engineering constructions is
explain: Line and staff organization combines direct command with specialist advisory support, making it most suitable and popular for civil engineering construction.

q: 82. Critical path
explain: The critical path is generally the longest path through the network; among the options given it 'may be longest' as it corresponds to the answer key.

q: 83. Henry Gant developed bar chart in
explain: Henry Gantt developed the bar chart technique around 1900, well before CPM/PERT were developed.

q: 84. Bar chart is suitable for
explain: Bar charts are simple and versatile, suitable for representing schedules of projects of all sizes - major and minor alike.

q: 85. Site order book is used for recording
explain: The site order book is maintained specifically to record instructions given by executive/supervising engineers to site staff/contractor.

q: 86. Various activities of a project, are shown on bar charts by
explain: In a bar chart, each activity is represented by a horizontal bar/line whose length is proportional to its duration.

q: 87. Which of the following documents should be prepared and submitted by a contractor?
explain: The bid document is prepared and submitted by the contractor in response to a tender notice.

q: 88. The first method invented for planning projects, was
explain: The bar chart (Gantt chart) method, invented in the late 1800s, was the earliest project planning tool, preceding milestone charts, CPM, and PERT.

q: 89. PERT analysis is based on
explain: PERT analysis uses all three time estimates - optimistic, pessimistic, and most likely - to compute the expected activity duration.

q: 90. The performance of a specific task in CPM, is known
explain: In CPM, the performance of a specific task is termed an activity.

q: 91. Completion of an activity on CPM network, is generally known
explain: In CPM networks, the point of completion (or start) of an activity is represented as a node.

q: 92. The artificial activity which indicates that an activity following it, cannot be started unless the preceding activity is complete, is known as
explain: A dummy activity is an artificial, zero-duration link used to enforce correct dependency/precedence relationships in the network.

q: 93. A dummy activity
options: is represented by a dotted line
explain: A dummy activity is artificially introduced, shown as a dotted arrow, and consumes no time - all characteristics apply.

q: 94. The estimated time required to perform an activity, is known as
explain: Duration is the estimated time needed to complete an activity.

q: 95. The difference between the time available to do a job and the time required to do the job, is known as
explain: Float (slack) is defined as the difference between available time and required time for completing an activity.

q: 96. Latest start of an activity is always
options: greater than or equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than or equal to latest event time of preceding node
equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than latest event time of preceding node
explain: The latest start time of an activity must be less than or equal to the latest allowable event time at its preceding node to avoid delaying the project.

q: 97. The critical activity has
explain: By definition, a critical activity has zero total float, since any delay would push back the overall project completion.

q: 98. The time by which activity completion time can be delayed without affecting the start of succeeding activities, is known as
explain: Free float is the amount of delay possible in an activity without affecting the earliest start of any succeeding activity.

q: 99. For completion of a project, the critical path of the network represents
explain: The critical path determines the minimum time in which the entire project can be completed.

q: 100. Which one of the following represents an activity
explain: All listed tasks (curing concrete, setting a question paper, preparing breakfast) are processes that take time and resources, hence all represent activities.

q: 101. Which one of the following represents an event?
explain: 'Concrete cured' denotes a completed state/milestone (an instantaneous occurrence), representing an event rather than an ongoing process.

q: 102. Critical path lies along the activities having total float
explain: Activities on the critical path always have zero total float by definition.

q: 103. The time which result in the least possible construction cost of an activity, is known
explain: (May be wrong )As per book Normal time is the duration at which the activity's direct cost is minimum (most economical execution pace).

q: 104. If t0, tp and tm are the optimistic, pessimistic and most likely time estimates of an activity respectively, the expected time t of the activity will be
explain: The PERT expected time formula is te = (t0 + 4tm + tp)/6, giving greatest weight to the most likely time.

q: 105. The figure below is used to indicate (merge symbol where multiple arrows converge into one node)
explain: When multiple activity arrows converge into a single node, this is called a merge event.

q: 106. The figure below is used to indicate (burst symbol where one node diverges into multiple arrows)
explain: When a single node diverges into multiple activity arrows, this is called a burst event.

q: 107. The technique for establishing and maintaining priorities among the various jobs of a project, is known
explain: Critical ratio scheduling is the specific technique used to set and maintain job priorities based on time remaining versus work remaining.

q: 108. PERT is
options: used for research and development projects
based on three time estimates for activities linking up two events
explain: PERT is event-oriented, commonly used for R&D projects with uncertain durations, and relies on three time estimates linking events - all statements are true.

q: 109. CPM is
options: is built of activities oriented programme
explain: CPM synthesizes project activities into an integrated program, is activity-oriented, and suits repetitive construction-type work - all apply.

q: 110. CPM family includes
explain: The CPM family of techniques includes Critical Path Analysis, Critical Path Plotted diagrams, and Critical Path Scheduling variants - all the above.

q: 111. In CPM analysis,
explain: CPM emphasizes activities, assumes deterministic (certain) durations, and represents activities as arrows - all statements are correct.

q: 112. Residential buildings are treated as
explain: Residential buildings, being relatively small-scale structures, are classified as light construction.

q: 113. Power stations are generally treated as
explain: Power stations, involving heavy machinery and large-scale industrial processes, are classified under industrial construction.

q: 114. A concrete mixer is specified by
options: the volume of the mixing drum
Volume of mixed concrete discharged after mixing of each batch
explain: A concrete mixer's specification includes drum volume, drum speed, and output volume per batch - all these parameters together specify it.

q: 115. In PERT analysis, the time estimates of activities and probability of their occurrence follow
explain: PERT assumes activity time estimates follow a Beta distribution, which allows for skewness between optimistic and pessimistic estimates.

q: 116. Which of the following does not represent an activity?
options: the office area is being cleaned
explain: 'Site located' is a state/point in time (an event), not a time-consuming activity like the other options.

q: 117. Total float for any activity is defined as the difference between
options: its latest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
its latest start time and earliest start time
its latest start time and earliest finish time
its earliest finish time and earliest start time for its successor activity
explain: Total float is calculated as the difference between an activity's latest start time and its earliest start time (or equivalently, LFT - EFT).

q: 118. If TL is the latest allowable event occurrence time, total activity slacks (S), is equal to
explain: Total float/slack can be equivalently computed as LST-EST, LFT-EFT, or TL-EFT, all giving the same result - so all of the above is correct.

q: 119. All the following are valid for CPM except
options: the beginning and end of an activity is denoted by nodes
explain: CPM assumes deterministic, certain activity durations; allowing uncertainties is NOT valid for CPM (that characteristic belongs to PERT).

q: 120. Which of the following represent an activity?
explain: Construction of foundation, roof, and superstructure are all time- and resource-consuming tasks, hence all represent activities.

q: 121. Earliest finish of an activity is always
options: greater than earliest event time of the following node
less than earliest event time of the following node
less than or equal to earliest event time of the following node
greater than or equal to earliest event time of the following node
explain: The earliest finish time of an activity must be less than or equal to the earliest event time of the node it leads into (since the node's earliest time is set by the latest-finishing predecessor).

q: 122. In the network shown in Fig., activity 4-5 can be started only when
explain: From the given network, node 4 is reached only after both activities 2-4 and 3-4 are complete, so activity 4-5 requires both to finish first.

q: 123. In PERT technique, completion of an activity is called
explain: In PERT, the completion point of an activity is termed the head event.

q: 124. Which of the following is a PERT event?
explain: 'Concreting of roof completed' denotes an instantaneous milestone/state, qualifying as a PERT event, unlike the ongoing transport/formwork processes.

q: 125. The technique which is activity oriented is
explain: CPM is activity-oriented, focusing on individual activities and their durations, unlike PERT which is event-oriented.

q: 126. Which one of the following represents an event?
explain: 'Concrete cured' represents a completed milestone/state (an event), while the others describe ongoing activities.

q: 127. Which of the following is an activity
explain: Even though phrased in past tense, all listed processes (curing, plastering, excavation) originally represent work/tasks consuming time - so all of the above per the answer key.

q: 128. Free float is mainly used to
options: identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total of preceding activity
identify the activities, which can be delayed without affecting the total float of succeeding activity
identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total float of either the preceding or succeeding activities
explain: Free float specifically identifies how much an activity can be delayed without affecting the float or start of the succeeding activity.

q: 129. The formula for determination of price adjustment in a work contract may not contain
explain: Price adjustment formulas typically use contract price, adjustment amount, and material/labour price indices, but do not directly include equipment cost as a variable.

q: 130. Select the correct statement
options: Activity arrows in a CPM network are drawn to scale
The tail of an arrow represents the finish of an activity
Arrow head represents the start of an activity
explain: All three statements are incorrect: arrows aren't drawn to scale, the tail represents the start (not finish), and the arrowhead represents the finish (not start).

q: 131. The direct cost of a project with respect to normal time is
explain: At normal time, the project is executed at its most economical pace, making direct cost minimum (it rises if crashed, i.e., time reduced below normal).

q: 132. Bidding document is prepared
explain: Bidding documents must be finalized and prepared before the tender notice is published so bidders can obtain and use them.

q: 133. The activity which is crashed first has
options: crashing has no relation with cost slope
explain: Crashing follows a least-cost approach, starting with the critical activity having the least (lowest) cost slope to minimize the additional cost incurred.

q: 134. Security deposit deducted from contractor's bill is
options: refunded when the contractor has completed the work
refunded even before the completion of the work provided good progress has been established
retained till the expected life of the structure of say 100 years and spent for maintenance
refunded when the defect liability period is over
explain: Security deposit is retained as protection against defects and is refunded only after the defect liability period expires satisfactorily.
